description: Trace fibonacci(4) through its recursive calls on n - 1 and n - 2 down to the base case n <= 1.

steps.description: In fibonacci(int n), check the base case if(n <= 1) on line 3 and return 1 on line 4 so the recursion stops when n reaches 1 or 0.
In the else branch on line 6, return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2), and call fibonacci(4) from main on line 11.

steps.answer: fibonacci(4) calls fibonacci(3) and fibonacci(2), and fibonacci(3) also calls fibonacci(2) and fibonacci(1), so fibonacci(2) is evaluated twice and ans receives 3 + 2 = 5.
steps.question: When main calls fibonacci(4), how many times does the program evaluate fibonacci(2), and what value is stored in ans?
